extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing Stage 1 and Stage 2 Registered Reports for submission to PCI Registered Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing, submitting, and revising Stage 1 (protocol) and Stage 2 (completed study) Registered Reports to PCI Registered Reports, covering methodological, ethical, transparency, and procedural requirements across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1A. The scientific validity of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: This criterion addresses the extent to which the research question is scientifically justifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid questions usually stem from theory/mathematics, application, or existing evidence; should be defined with sufficient precision to be answerable through quantitative or qualitative research; should fall within established ethical norms. Subjective judgments about importance, novelty or timeliness are NOT relevant to PCI RR assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1B. Logic, rationale, and plausibility of proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the coherence and credibility of any a priori hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses are not required; when present they should be stated precisely and follow directly from the research question or theory. Evaluates preliminary research/data reported at Stage 1 as part of this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1C. Soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses validity of study procedures and analyses, including critical design features and appropriateness of analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes internal/external validity, blinding, randomisation, rules for data inclusion/exclusion, suitability of pilot data. For inferential statistics, includes rigour of sampling plan (e.g., statistical power analysis or Bayesian alternative) and rationale for priors or smallest effect size of interest. For programmatic RRs, assesses whether components justify separate Stage 2 outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1D. Clarity and degree of methodological detail to enable replication and prevent undisclosed flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the Stage 1 protocol contains enough detail to closely replicate procedures and analyses and to prevent undisclosed flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods sections will generally be longer and more detailed than regular manuscripts; should clearly link research questions, hypotheses, sampling plans, analysis plans, and contingent interpretations. Authors are encouraged to include a design summary table. Blinded analyst approaches acceptable if specified in reproducible detail and blinding is robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1E. Consideration of outcome-neutral conditions (positive controls, quality checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether authors pre-specify outcome-neutral checks that reveal whether results are able to test the hypotheses or answer the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-neutral tests must be pre-specified and independent of main hypotheses (e.g., positive controls, manipulation checks, parallel measurements). Not always possible/applicable depending on design. Example provided (Galileo spacecraft study) as signature positive control.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2A. Whether the data are able to test the proposed hypotheses by passing approved outcome-neutral criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 2, evaluates if the obtained data meet the pre-specified outcome-neutral tests (e.g., absence of floor/ceiling effects, success of positive controls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of crucial outcome-neutral tests can, in severe cases, lead to Stage 2 rejection. This assessment is only relevant where outcome-neutral tests were pre-specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2B. Consistency of Introduction, rationale, and hypotheses with approved Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the Stage 2 submission's framing (introduction, rationale, hypotheses) matches the approved Stage 1 submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable changes: tense updates (future → past), correction of typos/factual errors. All changes must be shown as tracked changes at Stage 2; authors must submit a tracked-changes version. No substantive changes to research question, rationale, or hypotheses allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2C. Adherence to registered study procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses compliance with the preregistered protocol and treatment of deviations after IPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult the recommender immediately if deviations are needed before data collection completion. Minor changes may be permitted at recommender's discretion and reported at Stage 2. Major changes require withdrawal/resubmission to Stage 1. All preregistered analyses' outcomes must be reported except in rare jointly agreed cases of logical flaw; such analyses must still be mentioned in Methods with justification if omitted in Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2D. Justification and soundness of any unregistered exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses quality, justification, and informativeness of additional (post-IPA) unregistered analyses reported at Stage 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploratory/unregistered analyses are admissible but must be clearly identified (e.g., separate heading), justified, and caveated. Authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on unregistered analyses. Authors are not obliged to run additional tests suggested by Stage 2 reviewers unless necessary to meet Stage 2 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2E. Whether the authors' conclusions are justified by the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether claims and conclusions drawn by the authors are warranted by the data/evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to conclusions in Discussion, Abstract, and elsewhere. PCI RR decisions will not be based on importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence thresholds: general policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR does not set a universal evidence threshold due to disciplinary heterogeneity; expects field-appropriate rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should plan to obtain strength of evidence considered rigorous in their field. Reviewers will assess sufficiency on a case-by-case basis under criterion 1C. Authors aiming for PCI RR-friendly journals should meet those journals' minimum evidential requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence thresholds: Neyman–Pearson inference and power analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For fields using Neyman–Pearson inference, Stage 1 submissions should include an a priori statistical power analysis with justified estimated effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power analysis should use conservative (lowest available/meaningful) effect-size estimates because publication bias inflates published estimates. In cases of uncertainty, variable sample sizes and interim data analysis may be used with pre-specified inspection points, appropriate Type I error correction for peeking, and a final stopping rule. Tools suggested include G*Power, ANOVAPower, PANGEA, SIMR, and custom simulation approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence thresholds: Bayes factors and Bayesian methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For Bayesian analyses involving Bayes factors, authors must specify the predictive distribution for the theory and how its parameters are set, and aim for a useful strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of specification: uniform up to max, normal/half-normal to represent likely effect size, or JZS/Cauchy with a specified scaling constant. If stopping depends on Bayes factor, indicate a maximum feasible sample size after which sampling stops regardless of Bayes factor. Consult recommended readings for Bayes Factor Design Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence thresholds: alternative approaches for non-hypothesis-testing studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where studies do not use hypothesis testing, authors should propose alternative methods to establish evidence thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include planning for sufficiently precise parameter estimates or confidence intervals, or other discipline-appropriate standards; authors may propose bespoke analytic approaches or simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4 Ethics approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that research requiring ethics/IRB approval should generally have approvals in place before Stage 1 submission, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR may perform Stage 1 review before ethics approval in some cases; any IPA will be provisional pending confirmation of ethics approval. Provisional IPA is insufficient for PCI RR-friendly journals, which require ethics approval in place. Authors planning Stage 1 before approval should consult Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.5 Funding approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should generally ensure sufficient funding/resources are in place before Stage 1 submission, with two noted exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) exceptional public-interest or targeted funding circumstances where provisional IPA may be issued pending funding confirmation; (2) Registered Reports Funding Partnerships (RRFPs) where funders and PCI RR may review concurrently and funding can be awarded at the time IPA is given. Authors considering Stage 1 before funding should consult the Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.6 Levels of bias control for submissions involving existing data (Levels 1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy defining bias-control levels depending on whether data already exist and degree of authors' prior access/observation of key variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Level 6 = data do not yet exist (primary RRs); Levels 1–5 = varying degrees of prior access/observation with specified mitigations. Submissions must be Level 1 or higher to be eligible. If authors have observed data/variables/analyses to different extents, the article is assigned the lowest applicable level. Lower levels typically require more stringent countermeasures (conservative thresholds, blinded analyst, multiverse/specification analyses). PCI RR will not consider studies where authors already know prospective analysis outcomes (Level 0 would be ineligible). Authors must indicate which level applies; some PCI RR-friendly journals may require higher minimum levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.7 Use and reporting of preliminary and pilot studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include preliminary studies in Stage 1 to establish questions, generate hypotheses, estimate effect sizes, or demonstrate feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary studies strengthen submissions but must be clearly distinguished from preregistered protocol and will be published in Stage 2. Prospectively proposed research must be able to answer the question independently of preliminary outcomes; reliance on preliminary results for conclusions risks rejection under 1A/1B/1C.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.8 Protocol preregistration and embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR will preregister approved Stage 1 manuscripts on behalf of authors using OSF once IPA is granted; authors may choose a private embargo of up to 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR preregisters the approved manuscript unchanged after IPA. Authors must agree that if they withdraw after IPA, PCI RR may lift embargo and publish a short summary. Stage 2 abstracts must include the URL to the preregistered Stage 1 protocol and the date of in-principle acceptance. Clinical trials should still proceed with regular trial registration as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.9 Inclusion and labeling of registered and unregistered analyses at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered analyses' outcomes must be reported; unregistered analyses are admissible but must be clearly identified and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered analyses should be placed under headings like 'Exploratory analyses' and appropriately caveated; conclusions should not be based entirely on unregistered analyses. Additional unregistered studies are NOT permitted at Stage 2; adding further studies requires Incremental Registration (Section 2.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.10 Protocol deviations and required handling at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from the approved procedures after IPA could lead to rejection at Stage 2 unless handled per policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult the recommender immediately before completing data collection if deviations are needed. Scientific-essential, low-bias changes may be approved and reported with explanation (what, why, when, and recommender approval). Substantial changes require resubmission to Stage 1. All textual changes to approved parts must be highlighted as tracked changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.11 Data and materials transparency (TOP compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR requires authors to make study data, digital materials, and code publicly available at Stage 2 to the maximum extent permitted by law/ethics, consistent with TOP guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the PCI RR TOP guidelines before Stage 1. Badges (Open Data, Open Materials, Preregistered) are awarded per TOP policy (Section 2.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.12 Withdrawn registrations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy for withdrawal of manuscripts after IPA, including public recording of withdrawal and embargo handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR will mark Stage 1 recommendation as 'withdrawn' with a statement of facts/reasons; private embargoes will be lifted. Partial withdrawals generally not allowed except in programmatic RRs where components are separate Stage 2 outputs. Authors must provide estimated Stage 2 submission dates; failure to submit within 6 months of agreed deadline while unresponsive may lead PCI RR to consider the manuscript withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.13 Incremental registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism allowing authors to add further studies to an accepted registered plan via Incremental Registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who wish to add further studies at Stage 2 must use Incremental Registration rather than including additional unregistered studies in the Stage 2 manuscript. (Full procedural details in Section 2.13.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Registered Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for programmatic RRs for large or long-term research programmes with multiple components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic RRs will be assessed on whether separate study components are sufficiently robust to justify separate Stage 2 outputs. Components planned as separate Stage 2 outputs may be withdrawn independently without affecting IPA of remaining components; each remaining output must link to Withdrawn Registrations of withdrawn components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design summary template and study design expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a design summary table making explicit links between question, hypotheses, sampling, analyses, and interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.16 provides examples and templates; clear and accessible structure is expected to satisfy criterion 1D.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.18 Open review and anonymous review
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR publishes all reviews for recommended manuscripts; reviewers may sign or remain anonymous with some exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Stage 1 and 2 reviews and recommender decision letters are published no later than Stage 2 acceptance. Reviews of rejected submissions are not published. Managing Board members acting as reviewers must sign reviews. Authors may submit anonymously at Stage 1 by removing nominative information and sharing files via an anonymous URL; Stage 2 anonymous submission is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.19 Recommender triage
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial evaluation by recommenders to determine if submissions meet or nearly meet review criteria before specialist peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that meet/nearly meet criteria are sent for specialist peer review. Submissions that fail but have potential may be desk-rejected with invitation to resubmit and specific revision suggestions. Submissions substantially short will be desk-rejected outright.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.20 Standard review vs Scheduled review tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: Two tracks for Stage 1 peer review: Standard (full manuscript) and Scheduled (one-page snapshot leading to scheduled peer review dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard review takes ~4–8 weeks for first round. Scheduled review uses a 1-page snapshot template; if deemed suitable the recommender arranges a concentrated review week at least 6 weeks in future while authors prepare full manuscript. Scheduled review can significantly accelerate the first round but requires use of the provided template and advance planning (especially if Level 6 is chosen).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.21 Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited appeals process for authors rejected by PCI RR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be emailed within 30 days and must show either (a) factual errors by reviewers/recommender that materially affected decision, or (b) substantiated unfair treatment/bias. Appeals meeting criteria are reviewed by a panel (recommender + two Managing Board members) and decided by majority vote; other appeals are denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.22 Word limits and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR imposes no word limits or specific formatting requirements, but manuscripts should be concise and comprehensive in methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow disciplinary formatting conventions. Authors aiming for PCI RR-friendly journals should note those journals' formatting or word limits (not required for PCI RR recommendation but may be needed for journal adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.23 Badges for Open Practices and TOP Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR awards Open Data, Open Materials, and Preregistered badges per its TOP policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges will appear alongside the abstract for recommended Stage 2 RRs. Authors should consult the PCI RR TOP guidelines policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.24 CRediT taxonomy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT) to transparently acknowledge author contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Stage 2 manuscripts MUST include a CRediT statement. Use at Stage 1 is encouraged but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.25 How to submit (anonymous and non-anonymous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for submission, including how to submit anonymously at Stage 1 by posting materials to a repository providing an anonymous URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow instructions in Help > How to...? and platform-specific guides (OSF, GitHub). For anonymous submissions remove nominative information and share via anonymous URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.26 Revising and resubmitting: response expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must respond to all reviewer and recommender comments in a point-by-point format and provide revised manuscript with track changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A track-changes version must be available to reviewers and recommender either by uploading to PCI RR system or linking to a tracked version in a repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.27 Policy for a deceased co-author
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for retaining a deceased co-author after Stage 1 submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a footnote/acknowledgement stating the deceased author's contribution, the stage they were involved, that all co-authors consent to naming them, and that PCI RR (and journal if applicable) were informed and agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.28 Use of artificial intelligence for article writing and software code generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing acceptable use of AI tools in manuscripts and code, including disclosure, authorship, and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed uses: translation, correction, improvement of text or code if authors review/approve. AI may be used for data analysis if methods are published/cited/adequately described. AI cannot be listed as an author. When AI is used to generate text/code/illustrations authors must (a) carefully check for plagiarism, hallucinations, and errors, and (b) disclose how AI was used in Methods or Acknowledgements. Authors must not generate illustrations using AI because of plagiarism concerns. Failure to comply may result in rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCI RR assessment excludes subjective importance/novelty judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective judgments about importance, novelty or timeliness of the research question are not relevant criteria for PCI RR and are not part of assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on scientific validity, methodological rigour, and adherence to protocol rather than perceived impact or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to indicate bias-control level and publication of that level
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must identify which PCI RR bias-control level (1–6) applies to their submission; this selection will be displayed next to the abstract if finally recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of the prospective component include different levels, the article is assigned the lowest level among them. Authors should be aware that adopting journals may impose higher minimum levels for automatic acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with PCI RR-friendly journals' additional procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR-friendly journals commit to accepting PCI RR recommendations without further peer review provided any additional procedural requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements may include disciplinary scope, word limits, minimum pre-planned evidential standards (power, alpha, Bayes factors), or minimum bias-control levels. Where scientific expert judgement is required to assess such conditions, the journal will accept PCI RR's judgement without further review. Authors should check adopter listings to ensure compliance if aiming for automatic journal acceptance.
